explanations.text:
# DECOMPILE

user asks for a file to decompile

ai harness [reads the file and writes the abstraction](compiler/cli/human/skills/human/SKILL.md:Explain) with [pins on the abstraction words](compiler/cli/human/skills/human/SKILL.md:Pins) that point an entity. 
ai harness shows the abstraction text and always stop. even if the user message sounded like approval.

user [says the word: map it.](compiler/cli/human/cmd_map.py:e1:cmd_map)

ai harness pipes the exact text into the [human map command using the CLI](compiler/cli/human/cmd_map.py:e1:cmd_map).
the cli verifies the new abstraction and it makes no claude call:
  [it checks the pins point at real code or files](compiler/cli/human/compiler.py:e1:build_anchors),
  checks no two pins share their words, [so there are no circular dependencies](compiler/cli/human/compiler.py:e1:check_cycle),
  check each block pin gets [its exact lines](compiler/cli/human/compiler.py:e1:block_spans).
  a refusal returns the error to the ai harness, which reads it, fixes the text, and runs again.
  words the user wrote himself go in with --verbatim: kept as they are.
    [a pin in them goes in like any pin](compiler/cli/human/cmd_map.py:e1:verbatim_record) when its target exists, and the other pins come after, with the [retext command](compiler/cli/human/compiler.py:e1:cmd_retext);
  a copy of them the verbatim, with the pins taken out, stays in the json. called the ["origin"](compiler/cli/human/compiler.py:e1:origin_of), so a later mending can be measured against it.
cli creates one new abstaction appended to human/abstraction_<path>.json, never updates
  
ai harness [reports](compiler/cli/human/skills/human/SKILL.md:Report): 
  the entry, its pins, the coverage,
  the warnings as if [human show](compiler/cli/human/compiler.py:e1:cmd_show) was run
